title: Symphony: Learning Realistic and Diverse Agents for Autonomous Driving Simulation

control_signal.value: No user-facing control stated. Agents are conditioned on a route-based goal sampled by a learned goal generator; the reference trajectory provides initial conditions.

control_mechanism.value: Hierarchical policy: goal generator proposes a fixed route goal fed to a goal-conditional policy and discriminator; parallel beam search prunes the least realistic half of branches by discriminator score, and results are distilled back.

base_model.value: Behavioural cloning or model-based GAIL (MGAIL) policies with hierarchical goal generation (+H) and parallel discriminator-pruned beam search (+TS).

datasets.value: Proprietary Waymo dataset (1.1M run segments, 30s at 15Hz) and Waymo Open Motion Dataset (64.5K 10s segments).

metrics.value: Collision rate, off-road time, ADE (realism); minSADE and a novel curvature Jensen-Shannon divergence (diversity).

controllability_evidence.value: No controllability experiment; evidence is realism and diversity. On proprietary data BC collision rate drops from 16.65% to 1.84% with tree search, and hierarchy restores diversity.

stated_limitations.value: Beam search improves realism but harms diversity through mode collapse. Future work: alternative pruning rules to shape simulation, driver persona goals, and more diversity metrics.

notes: Not a controllable-generation paper; goals and pruning serve realism and diversity. Future-work mention of shaping simulation via pruning rules is not a tested control. Family choice is a judgement call.
